decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

The refuse and recycling bins shall be stored at all times in the designated refuse storage area within the proposed building, other than on collection days where they will be wheeled out to the street.&nbsp;

<p>The development hereby permitted shall not proceed beyond damp proof course level until the following has been submitted to, and approved by, the Council:</p><p>(a) Balcony railings materials/details and any required privacy screening. The development must be carried out in accordance with those approved details prior to occupation and retained thereafter.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Railway noise and vibration emissions </p><p><b>PART A</b></p><p>The development hereby permitted shall not commence (excluding demolition and site preparation), until the applicant has submitted to be approved in writing by the local planning authority, a Noise and Vibration Insulation Plan. The plan shall be prepared by a suitably qualified acoustic consultant and shall:</p><p>(1) Demonstrate, through appropriate assessment and modelling, that the internal ambient noise levels for residential units will not exceed the standards set out in:</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(a) BS 8233:2014 Guidance on sound insulation and noise reduction for buildings, namely:</p><p style="margin-left: 50px;">(i) 35 dB LAeq,16hr (07:00–23:00) for living rooms and bedrooms</p><p style="margin-left: 50px;">(ii) 30 dB LAeq,8hr (23:00–07:00) for bedrooms</p><p style="margin-left: 50px;">(iii) 45 dB LAFmax not normally exceeded during the night in bedrooms</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(b) And external noise levels in private amenity areas not exceeding:</p><p style="margin-left: 50px;">(i) 55 dB LAeq,16hr (as a desirable upper limit in accordance with BS 8233:2014;&nbsp;</p><p>(2) Demonstrate that the development will achieve adequate protection against railway-induced vibration in accordance with:</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(a) BS 6472-1:2008 Guide to evaluation of human exposure to vibration in buildings – Part 1: Vibration sources other than blasting, ensuring that Vibration Dose Values (VDVs) do not exceed thresholds corresponding to the "Low probability of adverse comment" category.</p><p>(3) Include full details of all required mitigation measures, including but not limited to enhanced glazing specifications, acoustic ventilation, wall and floor constructions, and any vibration isolation systems.</p><p>(4) Indicative details of the mechanical ventilation required for heating and cooling purposes for each proposed unit and communal spaces.&nbsp;</p><p>The development shall be constructed and retained in accordance with the details hereby approved.&nbsp;</p><p><b>PART B</b></p><p>Prior to the first occupation of any residential unit, the applicant shall submit to and have approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority a Post-Completion Verification Report. The report shall be prepared by a suitably qualified acoustic consultant and shall:</p><p>(1) Confirm that the residential units have been constructed in full accordance with the approved Noise and Vibration Insulation Plan</p><p>(2) Include results of on-site noise and vibration testing demonstrating compliance with the internal and external noise limits, and the vibration thresholds, as set out in Part A</p><p>(3) Where required, identify any further remedial works necessary to meet the required standards, which shall be implemented prior to occupation</p><p>The development shall be constructed and retained in accordance with the details hereby approved.&nbsp;</p>

<p>The development hereby permitted may not commence until a biodiversity gain plan has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The biodiversity gain plan must include the following:</p><p>(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat;</p><p>(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</p><p>(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</p><p>(d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development; and </p><p>(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development either from the Council or a private entity.&nbsp;</p><p>The development shall be completed and operated in accordance with those approved details.&nbsp;</p>

The development hereby permitted shall not proceed beyond damp proof course level until full details of the proposed solar photovoltaic (PV) panels, including their layout, size, siting, and specification, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details and shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development, unless otherwise approved in writing by the local planning authority.&nbsp;

The development hereby approved shall be constructed and retained with a minimum built-in storage area per unit of 1.5 square metres for each one-bedroom, two-person unit, and 2 square metres for each two-bedroom, four-person unit. Each storage space shall have a minimum headroom floor to ceiling height of 1.5m.&nbsp;

Prior to the installation of any external air source heat pumps, mechanical ventilation, or plant (MHVP) equipment, details of the proposed screening or enclosure materials, including design, dimensions, finishes, and siting, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.&nbsp; The development shall be completed in accordance with those approved details prior to occupation and retained thereafter.

<p>Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved drawings, the development hereby approved shall not progress above damp proof course level until the following details have first been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority:</p><p>(a) details and samples of the materials to be used in the external surfaces of the buildings (facing materials for the buildings, windows/ doors/ curtain walling, entrance canopies), hard surfaces, and any means of enclosure;</p><p>(b) drawings to a 1:20 metric scale to show typical details of the elevations from all sides;</p><p>(c) details of proposed boundary treatment materials.&nbsp;</p><p>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details, samples and drawings so agreed and shall be retained as such thereafter.</p><p><br></p><p>&nbsp;</p>

The development hereby permitted shall not be commenced until surface water attenuation and storage works have been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details as so agreed and shall thereafter be retained.

The development hereby permitted shall not be commenced until a drainage plan demonstrating separate disposal for sewage and stormwater has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The development shall be constructed and retained in accordance with those approved details.&nbsp;

All hard landscaping shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part of the development or in accordance with a programme that has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing to be agreed. All soft landscaping works including planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the approved scheme of landscaping shall be carried out no later than the first planting and seeding season following the final occupation of the residential parts of the buildings, or the completion of the development, whichever is the sooner. Any existing or new trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development, die, are removed, or become seriously damaged, diseased or defective, shall be replaced in the next planting season, with others of a similar size and species, unless the local authority agrees any variation in writing.&nbsp;

<p>The development hereby approved shall not commence (including demolition and site clearance) until a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CEMP shall include, but not be limited to, the following details:</p><p>(a)	Site management and control measures;</p><p>(b)	Hours of construction and demolition work;</p><p>(c)	Noise and vibration control;</p><p>(d)	Protection of any nearby watercourses, stormwater and ground conditions;</p><p>(e)	Biodiversity and wildlife protection measures;</p><p>(f)	Community liaison procedures;</p><p>(g)	Emergency spill response plan.</p><p>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved CEMP at all times during demolition and construction works.</p>

<p>The development hereby approved shall not commence, including any works of demolition, until a Detailed Construction Logistics Plan has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority in accordance with the format and guidance provided by Transport for London – www.tfl.gov.uk. and by Network Rail. The Detailed Construction Logistics Plan shall provide for:</p><p>(a) Parking of vehicles of site operatives/visitors.</p><p>(b) HGV access to site – loading and unloading of plant and materials.</p><p>(c) Number of HGV’s anticipated.</p><p>(d) Storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development.&nbsp;</p><p>(e) Programme of work and phasing.&nbsp;</p><p>(f) Site layout plan.&nbsp;</p><p>(g) Highway condition (before, during, after).</p><p>(h) Measures to control dust and dirt during construction.</p><p>(i) Measures to protect railways infrastructure and to ensure safe and efficient operation of the railway during the construction period, in consultation with Network Rail.&nbsp;</p><p>(j) A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works.</p><p>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Detailed Construction Logistics Plan, or any amendment or variation to it as may be agreed in writing by the local planning authority.</p>

Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved plans, the development hereby approved shall not commence (excluding demolition and site preparation) until a scheme for the hard and soft landscaping of the development, to include details of the planting and hard surfacing material within the site boundary including the access routes proposed within the application site, has been submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority. Soft landscaping works shall include: planting plans (at a scale not less than 1:100), written specification of planting and cultivation works to be undertaken and schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers / densities and an implementation programme. The scheme shall also include details of the boundary treatment. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved scheme or any amendment or variation to it as may be agreed in writing by the local planning authority and maintained in accordance with the approved scheme.

<p>The development hereby approved shall not commence&nbsp;(excluding demolition and site preparation) until a final Fire Safety Statement is submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, this statement shall include details of how the development will function in terms of the following:
</p><p>(a) identify suitably positioned unobstructed outside space: </p><p>(i) for fire appliances to be positioned on </p><p>(ii) appropriate for use as an evacuation assembly point </p><p>(b) is designed to incorporate appropriate features which reduce the risk to life and the risk of serious injury in the event of a fire; including appropriate fire alarm systems and passive and active fire safety measures </p><p>(c) is constructed in an appropriate way to minimise the risk of fire spread 
</p><p>(d) provide suitable and convenient means of escape, and associated evacuation strategy for all building users 
</p><p>(e) develop a robust management strategy for evacuation which is to be periodically updated and published (details of how often this management strategy is to be reviewed and published to be included), and which all building users can have confidence in
</p><p>(f) provide suitable access and equipment for firefighting which is appropriate for the size and use of the development.
</p><p>The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity.&nbsp;</p>

The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until a scheme for the on-going management and maintenance of the soft and hard landscaping within the development, to include a landscape management plan, including long term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules for a minimum period of 5 years for all landscape areas, and details of irrigation arrangements and green roofs, has first been submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing to be agreed. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the scheme so agreed and shall be retained as such thereafter.&nbsp;

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until evidence of Secured by Design Certification is submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, or justification shall be submitted where the accreditation requirements cannot be met with confirmation of what measures have been installed to improve the safety and security of the development. Secure by design measures shall be implemented prior to occupation and the development shall be retained in accordance with the approved details.&nbsp;

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until further details of cycle parking, including full specification of the type of stand and dimensions of storage unit(s) have been submitted to, and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so agreed and shall be retained as such thereafter.&nbsp;

<p>Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, a Delivery and Servicing Plan (DSP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The DSP shall be prepared in accordance with Transport for London’s guidance or other relevant local or national best practice and shall include, but not be limited to, the following details:</p><p>(a) Times and frequency of all deliveries, collections, and servicing activities, including waste collection, in order to minimise impact on the highway network and residential amenity;</p><p>(b) Access and egress arrangements for delivery and servicing vehicles, including swept path analysis for the largest expected vehicle;</p><p>(c) Designated loading/unloading areas and how they will be managed and kept clear of obstructions;</p><p>(d) Measures to avoid conflict with pedestrian, cycle, and vehicular movement during peak hours;</p><p>(e) Restrictions on delivery vehicle size and routing, where necessary;</p><p>(f) Security and safety measures, including visibility, lighting, and interaction with building access points;</p><p>(g) Waste and recycling collection arrangements;</p><p>(h) Monitoring and review mechanisms, including contact details for the site management team and processes for addressing complaints or operational issues.</p><p>The approved DSP shall be implemented upon first occupation of the development and shall be adhered to in perpetuity unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.</p>

<p>Land contamination</p><p><b>PART A</b></p><p>The development hereby approved shall not commence, including any site clearance, groundworks, or other preparatory works, until a Site Investigation Assessment has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This assessment shall be prepared by a suitably qualified and competent person and shall be carried out in accordance with current best practice guidance, including the Environment Agency’s Land Contamination Risk Management framework. The Site Investigation Assessment shall comprise the following:</p><p>(1) A Preliminary Risk Assessment (Phase 1 Desk Study) to identify:</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(a) Potential sources of contamination,</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(b) Potential pathways, and</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(c) Potential receptors, forming a clear conceptual site model;</p><p>(2) Where the Preliminary Risk Assessment identifies potential risks that may affect the proposed development, a Phase 2 Intrusive Site Investigation shall be undertaken and included as part of the assessment. This shall provide:</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(a) Details of site investigations and sampling,</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(b) Assessment of the nature and extent of any contamination,</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(c) An updated risk assessment of potential impacts on human health, controlled waters, property, and the environment;</p><p>(3) Where the results of the Phase 2 Investigation confirm that remediation is necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall also be submitted, setting out:</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(a) The remediation objectives,</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(b) Proposed remediation measures,</p><p style="margin-left: 25px;">(c) Verification and monitoring procedures.</p><p><b>PART B</b></p><p>Prior to the first occupation of the development, where a Remediation Strategy has been approved pursuant to Part A, a Verification Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall:</p><p>(1) Confirm that all remediation works have been completed in accordance with the approved strategy;</p><p>(2) Include results of any required verification sampling, testing, and monitoring;</p><p>(3) Include photographic and documentary evidence of the works;</p><p>Otherwise, if the details pursuant to Part A do not identify the need for a Remediation Strategy, Part B may be discharged prior to commencement of works, including site clearance, groundworks, or other preparatory works, confirming that the site is suitable for the approved end use.</p>

<p>The development hereby permitted shall not commence (excluding demolition and site preperation) until full details of biodiversity enhancements for the site have been submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority. The enhancements shall include:</p><p>(a) the type, number and location of bat and bird boxes/bricks and/or swift boxes/bricks to be incorporated across the site.&nbsp;</p><p>(b) full details of the proposed green roof treatment, including roof build up, plant species mix(es) which should include twenty plus native flower species offering pollen and nectar from early spring to late autumn, together with an assessment of the sustainability of the roof to ensure adequate water provision/retention.&nbsp;</p><p>(c) Full details of measures to be taken to provide shelter and foraging for invertebrate species at ground level, in the external building walls, and within the green walls and green roof areas.&nbsp;</p><p>(d) Log piles and passageways for reptiles and hedgehogs through the site from the adjacent railway.&nbsp;</p><p>(e) Treatment of existing invasive plant species on the site.&nbsp;</p><p>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details as so agreed and maintained thereafter.&nbsp;</p>
The residential units shall be designed and constructed to ensure that mains water consumption does not exceed 105 litres per person per day.
description: Redevelopment of vacant site; construction of a five storey building comprising nine residential units (Class C3) with associated private amenity spaces; landscaping; refuse and cycle storage
site_name: Harrow Island Site, Land At Hailsham Drive
